texts.text: Component libraries

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Component libraries are the first big improvement you can bring to your team. They allow you to maintain branding and consistent styling without having to manually clean up each prototype to look like your product. Building a component library will take some up-front effort, but you’re also building reusable assets that will greatly improve the quality of your prototypes going forward and save you time after the initial investment.

texts.orig: Workflow 1: Baselines and forks
texts.text: Workflow 1: Baselines and forks

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Baselines and forks are an extension of the component libraries strategy. With components, you’re giving team members a head start by providing building blocks they can easily assemble into good-looking prototypes. “Baselines” go one step further, giving you a high-quality reproduction of your current product experience, allowing your team members to more easily experiment with new ideas using simple prompts. Forks build on this further, allowing you to duplicate a project and all of its contents without using any tokens, and keep you from screwing up your baseline.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It’s critically important to choose the appropriate fidelity for your prototype based on the context, and then set clear expectations with team members around that level of fidelity. For example, if you’re explaining an interaction to an engineer, mid-fi is totally fine, and it’s a waste of time to push past that. Whereas if you’re pitching your CEO on funding a new team that will require millions in new investment, a functional high-fi mock is probably worth the time.
